definition.note: The tube whose bore is a circular helix -- the spring or serpentine: h > 0 right-handed, h = 0 degenerates to the torus, h < 0 left-handed.  NOTE: the mirror file's H1 reads "Coild", a typo carried over from conversion; the page body is headed COIL.

construction.blocked_by: Not built as a named surface.  The shipped Darboux sweep (helical_surface_generator, DARBOUX mode with helical motion of a circle) produces circled helicoids, but its generatrix rides in the meridian plane, not perpendicular to the motion, so the tube-around-a-helix proper has no operator.
construction.resume: A tube of constant radius swept along a circular helix; either extend the Darboux generatrix orientation or reuse the tube machinery; the parametrization is in the cited mirror chapter.

provenance.definition: Not transcribed. The record exists to state that the surface is absent and why; a fabricated equation would be worse than a null.
sources: R. Ferreol, "Coil (Serpentin)", Encyclopedie des formes mathematiques remarquables, mathcurve.com; local mirror chapter ch1233_serpentin_2 (S:/data/math_art/references/websites/mathcurve/book/surfaces/ch1233_serpentin_2.md).
